newsitem.title: USA: American Shared ends merger talks.
newsitem.headline: American Shared ends merger talks.

text.p: American Shared Hospital Services said Monday it ended discussions with U.S. Diagnostic Inc regarding a merger of the companies, citing U.S. Diagnostics as "unable to proceed with negotiations within a reasonable time period and on satisfactory terms."

American Shared said in a release that in December 1996, it agreed in principle with U.S. Diagnostic to an acquisition in which American Shared shareholders would have received $2.25 in cash for each outstanding share.
In January 1997, the parties agreed to increase the purchase price to $2.40 in U.S. Diagnostic common stock, to achieve pooling accounting treatment for the transaction.

Soon thereafter, American Shared said, U.S. Diagnostic publicly disclosed that it was under investigation by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for various matters, which led to changes in senior management and a significant decline in its stock price.

American Shared and U.S. Diagnostic then announced the delay of their proposed merger, and finally, American Shared said the continued inability of U.S. Diagnostic to proceed with discussions led to the termination of negotiations.
